title: Schnirelmann's theorem: every integer n >= 2 is a sum of at most 30772 primes, after Schnirelmann 1933
abstract: A Lean 4 proof, with no unproved steps, of the theorem of L. Schnirelmann, Über additive Eigenschaften von Zahlen, Math. Ann. 107, 1933: the set of 0, 1 and the sums of two primes has positive Schnirelmann density, and so every integer n >= 2 is a sum of a bounded number of primes. The proof also gives an explicit bound: every n >= 2 is a sum of at most 30772 primes. Mathlib's file Mathlib/Combinatorics/Schnirelmann.lean lists the proof of Schnirelmann's theorem as a TODO; this entry gives it, for Mathlib's schnirelmannDensity, with an explicit constant. The constant 30772 is far weaker than the best known ones: Ramaré 1995 showed that every n >= 2 is a sum of at most 7 primes, and Helfgott's ternary Goldbach theorem gives at most 4. The point is a complete formal version of Schnirelmann's argument with every constant explicit. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed. The Lean code was written by an AI agent and is offered for human audit.
